confirmed.title: No unlock line (with the forge hint) when quest or Slayer experience crosses a level
confirmed.evidence: The unlock line is printed only inside grantXp (src/ui/playerActions.ts:76-79), and only for the levels between oldLvl and s.lvl of that one call. Quest XP (claimQuest) and Slayer per-kill and bounty XP (adventure.ts:681 and 687) go through grantExactXp (adventure.ts:501-514). That function sets skill.lvl directly and prints nothing. The next grantXp call then starts from the already raised level, so the skipped levels are never announced. Neither claimQuestReward (playerActions.ts:466) nor handleMonsterDeath (actions.ts:256) prints anything for these levels. The code follows plan U2 literally, so the gap is in the spec, but it breaks the owner's condition on the 10x markup (design 7.1 item 7): show the forge recipe when a piece becomes wearable.
confirmed.scenario: A new character finishes the chain. The chain forces a goblin task. The six task kills give about 6 x 11.2 combat XP + 6 x 12 Slayer XP + an 80 XP bounty, roughly 219 Attack XP, which is Attack 3. Claiming Lumbridge Foundations then adds 250 Attack XP through grantExactXp, reaching 469 XP, past the 388 that Attack 5 needs. Attack jumps from 3 to 5 with no 'Level 5 Attack unlocks: Iron Scimitar (shop 1,400 GP, or forge: 2 Iron Bar at Smithing 5)' line, at the exact moment the shop-or-forge choice starts. Later bounties (160 to 700 Attack XP) can cross Attack 10, 20, 30 or 40 the same way and hide those weapon lines too.
confirmed.fix: In claimQuestReward and in handleMonsterDeath (after registerKill), record each skill's level before the call. After it, run the same loop grantXp uses: for each new level, unlockLine(meta.name, level, unlocksAt(skill, level)), then addChatMessage. Put this in one small helper in playerActions.ts that grantXp also uses. src/state cannot print chat, so it stays out of grantExactXp. Add a test that claims 'lumbridge' from Attack 3 and expects the Attack 5 line.

check.reason: I could not refute it; the code works as the finding says. grantExactXp (src/state/adventure.ts:501-514) only adds XP and recomputes skill.lvl. It updates HP and prayer, but it prints no chat line, no level-up message and no banner. Three places use it: claimQuest (line 626, for every quest XP reward), and registerKill for Slayer kill XP (line 681) and the bounty (line 687). The unlock lines come only from grantXp (src/ui/playerActions.ts:74-79), and only for the levels between oldLvl and the new level within that one call. So levels already reached through grantExactXp are never announced afterwards. Neither caller fills the gap. claimQuestReward (playerActions.ts:466-478) prints only the quest-complete chat and banner. handleMonsterDeath (src/engine/actions.ts:249-282) prints only Slayer progress and the bounty message. The numbers in the data back the scenario. The goblin band gives killXp 12 and bountyXp 80, Lumbridge Foundations gives 250 Attack XP, and the Iron Scimitar needs Attack 5 and can be forged with 2 iron_bar at Smithing 5. The exact total from combat XP depends on the attack style, but 250 quest XP on top of early combat XP can carry Attack past 388 XP (level 5) silently, and the larger bounties of 160 to 700 XP can do the same at higher tiers. The effect is limited to a missing chat or UI notice: the item can still be bought or forged, and nothing in the game state is wrong. The owner made the forge hint a condition of the 10x markup, and the miss happens on the main new-player path, so medium is the right severity rather than high.
